sources.title: 16 CFR 255.5 - Disclosure of material connections
sources.method: fetched 2026-11-20; re-fetched during the final integration pass. The eCFR reports Title 16 up to date as of 11/18/2026 and the section's source as 88 FR 48102 (July 26, 2023). Example 11 of 255.5 is the affiliate-link case: a blogger who reviews coffee makers and earns a share of sales must clearly and conspicuously disclose the compensation.
sources.used_for: Why the disclosure sits above the fold on every page: a material connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously, and an affiliate commission is a material connection (Example 11).
sources.quote: 'Because knowledge of this compensation could affect the weight or credibility site visitors give to the blogger's reviews, the reviews should clearly and conspicuously disclose the compensation.' - 16 CFR 255.5, Example 11.

sources.title: Associates Central Help: What is the application review process?
sources.method: fetched in full 2026-11-20
sources.used_for: The published bar an Associates application is reviewed against: qualified sales (at least three in the first 180 days), Sites that are publicly available, at least 10 posts of robust original content, and website content recent within roughly 60 days.
sources.quote: 'our Associates team will check your application once you've driven qualified sales (we require at least three within the first 180 days)' and 'All Sites must have robust original content (even when advertising is removed) - a good rule of thumb is at least 10 posts' and 'Content on your website must be recent (generally within the last 60 days). You must own your website.'
